flashcards.front: What is the primary threat vector for AI-Augmented Cyberattacks?
flashcards.back_definition: Adversaries exploit synthetic voice cloning on audio credentials to bypass standard perimeter security controls.
flashcards.back_example: Example: SIP Trunk Alert: Spectral coherence mismatch on caller ID
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse this threat with other layers (like physical breaches or certificate revocations) which target different assets.
flashcards.back_hook: Recall: synthetic voice cloning is the unlocked door; audio credentials is what the attacker wants to steal.

flashcards.front: How does the security team mitigate AI-Augmented Cyberattacks threats?
flashcards.back_definition: Deploying and enforcing out-of-band security challenges and acoustics auditing directly hardens audio credentials and blocks unauthorized connections.
flashcards.back_example: Action: Update security configurations to require out-of-band security challenges and acoustics auditing.
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse mitigation (actively blocking the exploit) with detection (simply logging or alerting the event).
flashcards.back_hook: Mitigation is the shield; detection is the security camera.

flashcards.front: How do analysts detect exploitation of AI-Augmented Cyberattacks?
flashcards.back_definition: By auditing event data and implementing logic flags built to alert on voice spectrum frequency anomalies.
flashcards.back_example: Syslog trace: SIP Trunk Alert: Spectral coherence mismatch on caller ID
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse signature-based detection (matching known strings) with anomaly-based detection (mapping dynamic standard deviations).
flashcards.back_hook: Detection is looking for the fingerprint left behind by the threat.
